q: Crops grown primarily to be sold for export and commercial revenue (e.g. cocoa, rubber, oil palm) are ____. (P4)
explain: Cash crops generate national foreign exchange and significant income for farmers.
hint: Crops grown primarily for market sales.

q: The tree crop whose fermented and dried beans are processed into chocolate and cocoa beverage is ____. (P4)
explain: Cocoa (Theobroma cacao) is a major tropical agricultural export used worldwide for chocolate confectionery.

q: The white milky liquid (latex) tapped from the bark of the rubber tree is processed into ____. (P4)
explain: Coagulated latex yields natural rubber for tyres, footwear, and flexible industrial tubing.

q: Organic fertilizer made by decomposing plant waste, food scraps, and animal manure in a pit is ____. (P4)
explain: Compost restores soil organic matter, beneficial microbial activity, and moisture retention.

q: Insects (such as locusts, caterpillars, and weevils) that destroy crops and stored food grains are agricultural ____. (P4)
explain: Pests cause significant pre-harvest field loss and post-harvest granary destruction.

q: Crop classification: Yam is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 4).
explain: Yam is botanically classified as a tuber / root crop.

q: Crop classification: Cassava is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 4).
explain: Cassava is botanically classified as a tuber / root crop.

q: Crop classification: Rice is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 4).
explain: Rice is botanically classified as a cereal grain.

q: Crop classification: Millet is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 4).
explain: Millet is botanically classified as a cereal grain.

q: Crop classification: Sorghum (Guinea corn) is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 4).
explain: Sorghum (Guinea corn) is botanically classified as a cereal grain.

q: Crop classification: Cowpea (Beans) is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 4).
explain: Cowpea (Beans) is botanically classified as a legume.

q: Crop classification: Groundnut (Peanut) is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 4).
explain: Groundnut (Peanut) is botanically classified as a legume and oil crop.

q: Crop classification: Oil Palm is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 4).
explain: Oil Palm is botanically classified as a oil and cash crop.

q: Crop classification: Cotton is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 4).
options: fibre crop used for making textile clothing
explain: Cotton is botanically classified as a fibre crop used for making textile clothing.

q: Crop classification: Coffee is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 4).
explain: Coffee is botanically classified as a beverage crop.

q: Crop classification: Tea is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 4).
explain: Tea is botanically classified as a beverage crop.

q: Crop classification: Sugarcane is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 4).
explain: Sugarcane is botanically classified as a sugar crop.

q: Animal husbandry: What major agricultural products do we obtain from Sheep? [P4]
explain: Sheep provide wool and mutton for human consumption and industrial use.

q: Animal husbandry: What major agricultural products do we obtain from Bees (Apiculture)? [P4]
explain: Bees (Apiculture) provide honey and beeswax for human consumption and industrial use.

q: Animal husbandry: What major agricultural products do we obtain from Silkworm? [P4]
explain: Silkworm provide silk fibre for textiles for human consumption and industrial use.

q: Animal husbandry: What major agricultural products do we obtain from Pigs (Swine)? [P4]
explain: Pigs (Swine) provide pork and bacon for human consumption and industrial use.

q: Animal husbandry: What major agricultural products do we obtain from Goats? [P4]
explain: Goats provide chevon meat, milk, and leather for human consumption and industrial use.
